newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia state oil company sets 1997 targets. [CORRECTED 22:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Colombia state oil company sets 1997 targets. [CORRECTED 22:41 GMT]

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol will spend $1.08 billion on production and exploration in 1997, it announced in a statement Monday.

The company has set a target of drilling between 23 and 38 new exploration wells and said it is looking to boost production from the current level of about 642,000 barrels per day to 723,000 barrels per day by the end of 1997.
Although Ecopetrol will spend the bulk of its total $1.66 billion budget on exploration and production it said it would invest 268 billion pesos in refining and marketing.

Ecopetrol said in its press statement, "The largest investment will be in exploration and production in 1997. The priority for Ecopetrol is to strengthen direct exploration and production operations and association contracts (with private domestic and foreign companies)."

The company added that it would be looking to forge ahead in the production and sales of oil derivatives and boost the petrochemical industry. This it said could be done by reorganizing some activities at its refinery in Cartagena on the Caribbean coast to include primary petrochemicals production.
